pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: Severe abdominal pain without physical signs (pain out of proportion to exam) triggered by fasting, catastrophic neuro-psychiatric deterioration following P450-inducing drugs (Haloperidol/Metoclopramide), and urine turning a port-wine color upon exposure to air and light. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant metabolic disorder caused by a deficiency in hydroxymethylbilane synthase (PBG deaminase), an essential enzyme in the heme biosynthetic pathway. Caloric restriction (fasting) and cytochrome P450-inducing drugs severely upregulate hepatic ALAS1 enzyme activity. This leads to a massive accumulation of toxic porphyrin precursors: delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG). These neurotoxic metabolites cause widespread autonomic and peripheral neuropathies (leading to severe abdominal pain, ileus, tachycardia, and ascending motor paralysis) as well as central nervous system dysfunction (psychosis, seizures, SIADH causing hyponatremia). When urine containing excess PBG is exposed to light and air, PBG spontaneously polymerizes into porphobilin, turning the urine a characteristic port-wine dark red color.
